label: Real run on this Mac's Docker Compose stack, with synthetic traffic from klaxon.traffic: synthetic data, a simulated provider, no real money. One fault from klaxon.faults, duplicate-delivery, was injected on purpose. The alert was raised by klaxon.alerts from what the stack showed. Klaxon's loop ran live on it, through Claude Code on Aravind's seat, and stopped on diagnosed after 9 steps; any reply it got is a recorded response, not a simulation. It was offered one write action (rollback_deploy), as in week 4; in an evaluation run its gate only plans an action the diagnosis names: nobody is asked, and nothing runs. The diagnosis was compared with the fault's recorded cause by a rule (klaxon.grading), not by a person or a model. Code planned the action its diagnosis named (redeploy ledger-consumer: LEDGER_HANDLER naive -> idempotent, LEDGER_BAD_EVENTS dead_letter (unchanged)); in an evaluation run nobody is asked, and nothing ran. The fault's cause was removed by the harness's clearing (klaxon.faults).

diagnosis.hypothesis: At 10:40:48 ledger-consumer was redeployed with LEDGER_HANDLER=naive. That handler books a ledger transaction for every Kafka message and never checks whether the event_id was already posted. The provider resends webhooks until they are acknowledged, so webhook-receiver can put the same event on provider-events more than once. A correct handler skips those copies. The naive one books each copy. evt_000308 was queued and booked 3 times, and six other events were booked twice. The extra payment postings put provider_clearing $493.23 ahead of the provider. The doubled refund (evt_000288) pulls pay_000217 below the provider's figure. The ledger stays balanced because each duplicate is a full double entry. Payments and refunds still match the provider, so the damage is limited to the ledger. Still open: why the provider retried these webhooks. A slow acknowledgement or the container recreation are likely causes, but the ledger is meant to absorb retries either way.

evidence.shows: The symptom is real. posted_exactly_once fails with 7 events booked 2 or 3 times, and matches_provider is off by +$493.23. The ledger is balanced, and payments and refunds match the provider, so only the ledger is wrong.
ledger-consumer was redeployed at 10:40:48 with LEDGER_HANDLER=naive, 17s before the alert. No other service changed since 10:39:22.
ledger-consumer booked evt_000308 three times, from offsets 100, 101 and 103 on partition 0, between 10:41:02 and 10:41:04.
webhook-receiver queued evt_000308 three times at those same offsets. These are redeliveries of one event, which the ledger should have deduplicated.
evt_000251 was booked twice, at 10:40:49.0 and 10:40:49.7 from offsets 73 and 76, right after the naive-handler deploy.
ledger-consumer logs show only 'posted' lines, with no dedup or skip messages, which fits a handler that does not check event_id.

proposed_fix.summary: Roll ledger-consumer back to its settings before the 10:40:48 deploy. This should restore its idempotent handler and stop new duplicate postings. Then, as a separately approved data repair, reverse the extra ledger transactions: keep the first transaction for each duplicated event and reverse the rest. The known extras are 255, 265, 272, 273 and 297, plus the extras for evt_000298 and evt_000308 (two for evt_000308), found from the money check evidence. Rerun the money check afterwards.

diagnosis.blast_radius: Recreating ledger-consumer pauses ledger booking briefly. Kafka holds the events, so lag builds and then drains. payment-confirmer and payments-api are not touched. The rollback repairs nothing already booked: the ledger stays $493.23 off until the data repair runs.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: If the rolled-back handler misbehaves, for example by stalling or rejecting events, redeploy ledger-consumer with its current settings. Events wait in Kafka under its consumer group and are not lost. Any data-repair reversals can be undone with offsetting transactions.
